blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing participatory planning with no planning. Participatory planning still produces a CLUP and zoning ordinance; the difference is HOW they are developed—with genuine community involvement, not expert imposition.", "Assuming Advocacy Planning means planners are politically neutral. Davidoff argued that planners serving marginalized communities must actively advocate for their interests, not pretend neutrality favors the disadvantaged (it doesn't).", "Treating a single public hearing as sufficient participation. RA 7160 requires consultation, but meaningful participation involves multiple touchpoints, diverse engagement methods, and demonstrable influence on the final plan.", "Overlooking that design charrettes are different from public hearings. Charrettes are intensive, interactive design sessions where participants collaborate on concepts; hearings are one-way information presentation. Charrettes are more participatory."]} />
